sources.name: Legal 500: residence permit in Turkey by buying real estate
sources.says: Dated 29 August 2025. From 16 October 2023 "the assessed value of the property, as recorded in the cadastral registers, must not be less than 200,000 USD". The permit runs one to two years and is renewable while the property is kept. Since 1 July 2022 new applications have been barred in 1,169 neighbourhoods across 15 provinces. sources.name: Turk.Estate: residence permits in Turkey's "restricted" areas, which locations reopened in 2026
sources.says: Dated 12 June 2026, updated 11 November 2026. In early June 2026 Turkey opened almost all previously closed districts and e-ikamet began accepting applications across most of the country, through practice and not through a decree with a published list; the migration authority's closure pages still date from 2021 and 2022 and there is no updated public register. Antalya: Kepez and Altıntaş are named as open, parts of Konyaaltı and Muratpaşa as disputed. Istanbul: Avcılar, Beylikdüzü, Şişli, Beyoğlu and others are listed as available; Fatih and Esenyurt remain unconfirmed. A purchase from USD 200,000 carries the right to a residence permit, subject to the address check; USD 400,000 is the separate citizenship threshold.

claims.note: Also Antalya's summary and `why` ("a $200k property route"), which agree. The threshold dates from 16 October 2023 and a November 2026 page still gives USD 200,000. sources.name: Turk.Estate: residence permits in Turkey's "restricted" areas, which locations reopened in 2026
sources.says: Dated 12 June 2026, updated 11 November 2026. In early June 2026 Turkey opened almost all previously closed districts and e-ikamet began accepting applications across most of the country, through practice and not through a decree with a published list; the migration authority's closure pages still date from 2021 and 2022 and there is no updated public register. Antalya: Kepez and Altıntaş are named as open, parts of Konyaaltı and Muratpaşa as disputed. Istanbul: Avcılar, Beylikdüzü, Şişli, Beyoğlu and others are listed as available; Fatih and Esenyurt remain unconfirmed. A purchase from USD 200,000 carries the right to a residence permit, subject to the address check; USD 400,000 is the separate citizenship threshold.

sources.name: Hayat Estate: Turkey reopens almost all restricted districts for residence permits
sources.says: Dated 08.06.2026, citing local media reports and no official announcement. The e-ikamet system "has started accepting applications across almost the entire country again"; "only two districts in Istanbul remain closed to new applicants" (Fatih and Esenyurt).

sources.name: Rest Property: Turkey reopening closed districts for residence permits
sources.says: Dated 05.06.2026. "An official document was signed on June 2, providing for the reopening of several districts", but "official orders and departmental instructions have not yet been delivered to the local migration offices" and the list of locations "is still pending publication".

sources.name: Legal 500: residence permit in Turkey by buying real estate
sources.says: Dated 29 August 2025. From 16 October 2023 "the assessed value of the property, as recorded in the cadastral registers, must not be less than 200,000 USD". The permit runs one to two years and is renewable while the property is kept. Since 1 July 2022 new applications have been barred in 1,169 neighbourhoods across 15 provinces. Permanent residence is available after eight years of residence. Health insurance is required for applicants over 18 and under 65. It does not mention a USD 400,000 citizenship threshold.

also: summary: "many districts closed to new property permits" became "unclear rules on which districts accept new property permits"
drawback 3 reworded: "Which districts accept new property permits is unclear, and the tax regime is untested"
claims.note: As for Antalya. Hayat Estate says Fatih and Esenyurt remain closed; Turk.Estate says their status is unconfirmed; the profile says "reportedly not".

claims.claim: After a year of residence foreigners can join the state GSS scheme at 24% of the minimum wage, but it excludes pre-existing conditions, so top-up private cover is advised

sources.name: Ikamet: health care services for foreigners in Turkey
sources.says: Published December 26, 2020, last updated October 10, 2026. A foreigner can join the state scheme (GSS) after "living in Turkey for longer than a year"; premiums are 24% of the national minimum wage. Since 2017 the SGK "would not cover the costs of treatments and medicines for pre-existing conditions", so complementary insurance is recommended. "The prerequisite for obtaining a residence permit is to have private health insurance"; people over 65 need not buy it before the appointment.

claims.note: A secondary page updated October 2026; sgk.gov.tr was not read. The same page says private insurance is a condition of the permit, with over-65s exempt, which the profiles do not claim.

claims.claim: Private hospitals such as Medical Park, Memorial and Anadolu serve international patients with English-speaking staff

sources.name: Rest Property: expat life in Antalya 2026
sources.says: Dated 28.11.2025. Leading facilities are listed as Medical Park Antalya, Memorial Antalya Hospital and Anadolu Hospitals; "major private hospitals provide English-speaking staff". It does not use the words "international patients".

claims.note: Confirmed on the secondary page the profile cites (names, English-speaking staff). The hospitals' own sites could not be read: medicalpark.com.tr, memorial.com.tr (two URLs) and the ITIJ profile of Antalya Anadolu Hospitals returned 403. "Serve international patients" rests on the page's description of them as the leading private hospitals for expats; a search result (not a read) showed Memorial Antalya's international-patient services.

claims.claim: The Acıbadem and Memorial groups run several JCI-accredited Istanbul hospitals, and Istanbul-based Medipol runs 14 hospitals

sources.name: TB Mag: hospitals and medical tourism in Türkiye for international patients, 2026
sources.says: Dated 20/05/2026. Acıbadem "operates 23 hospitals and 17 clinics across Türkiye, with several JCI-accredited facilities in Istanbul". "Several Memorial hospitals in Istanbul have received JCI accreditation." Medipol, headquartered in Istanbul, "offers comprehensive care across 14 hospitals".

claims.note: A dated trade page; JCI's own directory and the groups' sites were not read.
